newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom declines comment on GlobalOne.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom declines comment on GlobalOne.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, the German telecommunications group, said on Thursday it would not comment on a report that losses at its GlobalOne venture with Sprint Corp and France Telecom were higher than expected.
"Traditionally we do not comment on speculation," Deutsche Telekom spokesman Hans Ehnert told Reuters.
GlobalOne officials at their European headquarters in Brussels also declined to comment.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom were trading lower in pre-bourse dealings and opened down 10 pfennigs at 30.15 marks in bourse trade in contrast to the DAX index of 30 blue-chips, which opened 0.67 percent higher.
Two sources close to GlobalOne told Reuters on Wednesday that the venture set up in January last year was expected to lose $250 million for 1996 but has in fact lost almost $370 million.
"The partners are furious about the losses. Word has come down that they are looking to cut jobs," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

Global One currently has 2,900 employees and has been spending heavily to build a network powerful enough for it to carry traffic for other telecom firms as well as to cater to the global needs of large businesses.
The partners have revealed no financial details about Global One's performance in 1996 except to say it is expected to end the year with more than $800 million of orders.
